method: ndisasm raw disassembly of the unnamed function at wpcmk file 0x59e0 (wpcmk_entry_and_roster_menu, per task spec). Cross-referenced with save-state memory reads via dosbox_read_memory MCP tool. Validated against 3 decoded DOSBox screenshots (tools/dosbox/save/1.sav, 2.sav, 3.sav).

findings.claim: wpcmk_entry_and_roster_menu is at file offset 0x59e0 in wpcmk.ovr. Ghidra has no named function there — the function ends at 0x5c03 (ret) and is surrounded by: wpcmk_show_roster_picker (0x56a0) before it and strcmp_2byte_step (0x5c42) after it. The function was not auto-analyzed by Ghidra, likely because the entry is only reached via the overlay dispatch stub at file 0x0010 (the wroot overlay-loader mechanism).

At 0x5a6e–0x5a8a, the function initializes a 6-entry enabled[] array on the stack (bp-0x26 through bp-0x1c) to all 1s via a loop from 0 to 5. This is the menu option enabled-state array, where 1=enabled and 0=disabled.

evidence.asm_excerpt:
5a6e: mov [bp-2], 0 // loop counter
5a73: mov ax,[bp-2]; shl ax,0; mov bx,ax; add bx,bp
5a7c: mov word [bx-0x26], 1  // enabled[counter] = 1
5a81: inc [bp-2]; cmp [bp-2], 5; jng 5a73  // loop 0..5

findings.claim: After initializing all to 1, the function calls roster_find_first_empty_slot (0x4ff4) and checks the return. If == -1 (roster FULL — no empty slot available), it sets enabled[0] = 0, disabling CREATE PC. Otherwise (at least one empty slot), CREATE PC remains enabled.

evidence.asm_excerpt:
5a91: call 0x4ff4 (roster_find_first_empty_slot)
5a94: cmp ax, -1
5a97: jnz 0x5a9e  // if NOT -1 (NOT full), skip disable
5a99: mov word [bp-0x26], 0  // enabled[0] = 0 -> disable CREATE PC

findings.claim: After the CREATE PC check, the function scans the occupancy array (DGROUP 0x4fd8..0x4fd8+slot_count) for any byte == 1. If no occupied slots are found (roster EMPTY), it sets enabled[1]=0, enabled[2]=0, enabled[3]=0, enabled[4]=0, disabling REVIEW PC, DELETE PC, RENAME PC, and PORTRAIT. EXIT (enabled[5]) is never disabled.

evidence.asm_excerpt:
5a9e: mov [bp-4], 0 (has_any_char=0)
5aa3: mov [bp-2], 0 (i=0)
5aaa: cmp byte [bx+0x4fd8], 1
5ab2: jnz 0x5ab9
5ab4: mov [bp-4], 1 (has_any_char=1)
5ab9: inc [bp-2]; cmp ax,[0x4fd2]; jl 5aaa
5ac5: mov ax,[bp-4]  // ax = has_any_char (0 or 1)
5ac8: mov [bp-0x24], ax  // enabled[1]
5acb: mov [bp-0x22], ax  // enabled[2]
5ace: mov [bp-0x20], ax  // enabled[3]
5ad1: mov [bp-0x1e], ax  // enabled[4]

findings.note: When has_any_char=0 (empty roster), options 1-4 are set to 0. When has_any_char=1, they're set to 1 (already 1 from initialization, so no visible change). EXIT (enabled[5]) is never touched by any conditional — it remains 1 always.

findings.claim: The 6 enabled[] slots map to options in this order: [0]=CREATE PC, [1]=REVIEW PC, [2]=DELETE PC, [3]=RENAME PC, [4]=PORTRAIT, [5]=EXIT. This is confirmed by the jump table at file 0x5bb6 (CS:0xa11a via the wpcmk overlay delta 0x4564) which maps selection results 0..4 to handlers, plus EXIT (case 5) handled directly by a range check.

jump_table_entries.action: jmp 0x5bcd (outer loop check; triggers exit) -> EXIT

evidence.delta_law: CS_offset = file_offset + 0x4564 (wpcmk overlay delta per CLAUDE.md)

findings.claim: The maximum roster slot count is 16 (0x10). This is the value at DGROUP 0x4fd2 (loaded from pcfile.dbs header +0x02). roster_find_first_empty_slot scans 0..*(0x4fd2)-1 = 0..15.
The 3 save states confirm the 3 roster conditions. Physical memory at DGROUP 0x4fd8 (occupancy array) and 0x4fd2 (slot_count=16) verified:

evidence.save_1_expected_options: all 6: CREATE PC + REVIEW PC + DELETE PC + RENAME PC + PORTRAIT + EXIT
evidence.save_3_expected_options: 5: REVIEW PC + DELETE PC + RENAME PC + PORTRAIT + EXIT (no CREATE PC)

findings.claim: The layout observed from decoded screenshots (tools/parity/decode-screen.ts output) for each state. The engine uses ui_menu_picker_vertical (0x29c) which lays out the enabled options. The screen renders options in 2 rows x 3 columns when 6 options, or different arrangements for fewer options.

evidence.save_2_empty_layout: 2 options (CREATE PC, EXIT) displayed centered at the bottom, one above the other (2 rows, 1 center column)
evidence.save_1_partial_layout: 6 options in 2x3 grid: row0=[PORTRAIT, CREATE PC, DELETE PC], row1=[EXIT, REVIEW PC, RENAME PC] — exact column assignment TBD by pixel measurement; matches task spec: row1 CREATE PC/DELETE PC/PORTRAIT, row2 REVIEW PC/RENAME PC/EXIT
evidence.save_3_full_layout: 5 options: EXIT (left), REVIEW PC/DELETE PC (center col, row0/row1), RENAME PC/PORTRAIT (right col, row0/row1)
evidence.note: Pixel-precise column positions are for a future parity pass. The current implementation should faithfully reproduce the OPTION SET per state; column positions are approximations from the decoded screenshots.

findings.note: Option set is high-confidence (RE-confirmed). Grid positions are approximate from decoded screenshots; exact positions require pixel measurement of the rendered windows.

findings.claim: The menu options' labels are sourced from msg.dbs starting at msg ID 0x46a: 0x46a=CREATE PC, 0x46b=REVIEW PC, 0x46c=DELETE PC, 0x046d=RENAME PC, 0x046e=PORTRAIT. EXIT has no msg ID and is rendered as a literal.

evidence.asm: push 0x46a  ; base msg ID passed to ui_menu_picker_vertical (0x29c)

option_rules.CREATE_PC: shown only when roster has at least one empty slot (rosterCount < MAX_SLOTS = 16)
option_rules.REVIEW_PC: shown only when roster has at least one character (rosterCount > 0)
option_rules.DELETE_PC: shown only when roster has at least one character (rosterCount > 0)
option_rules.RENAME_PC: shown only when roster has at least one character (rosterCount > 0)
option_rules.PORTRAIT: shown only when roster has at least one character (rosterCount > 0)
